objective.text: Recognize that filesystem append implemented as read-modify-write is not a concurrent logging guarantee.

difficulty.rationale: Recognize a lost-update risk that a convenient storage method does not eliminate.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

assumptions: Several worker processes append to the same object; no external lock or serialization exists.

stem: A design uses Storage::append for a shared audit trail because its method name sounds like an atomic append. What must the review account for?

options.text: The adapter can read and rewrite the object; concurrent writers need an appropriate serialization or logging design.
options.rationale: The filesystem adapter’s append implementation reads existing contents and writes the combined result; that is not a cross-process atomic-append guarantee.

options.text: Switching the disk from local to object storage guarantees atomic line appends.
options.rationale: Changing adapters does not give this generic read-and-rewrite helper an atomic line-append contract.
options.misconception: Changing adapters does not give this generic read-and-rewrite helper an atomic line-append contract.

options.text: append always acquires a distributed lock based on the object key.
options.rationale: The adapter does not automatically acquire a shared application lock around the read and write.
options.misconception: The adapter does not automatically acquire a shared application lock around the read and write.

options.text: Newline separation prevents two workers from overwriting each other’s changes.
options.rationale: Separators affect formatting, not concurrent read-modify-write interleavings.
options.misconception: Separators affect formatting, not concurrent read-modify-write interleavings.
